dedupe_keys.name: an integrated multi source dataset for measuring settlement evolution in the united states from 1810 to 2020

description: An Integrated Multi-Source Dataset for Measuring Settlement Evolution in the United States from 1810 to 2020 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Yoonjung Ahn et al. Understanding changes in the built environment can inform sustainable urban development and disaster preparedness. Recent years have seen the emergence of a variety of global, continent-level, and nation-wide datasets related to the current state and the evolution of the built environment, human settlements or building stocks. However, such datasets may face limitations like incomplete coverage, sparse building information, coarse resolution, and ... Coverage: global (US); published in 2024. Formats: GeoTIFF, TXT, Raster. The data are held in Harvard Dataverse and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 39740701. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
